text:
anna: Quick check — the cost sparkline on the Route Detail card is dipping below 0 for some routes when sticky-routing + prefetch is enabled. saw this in the customer demo this morning, not great. :grimacing:
raj: can you paste the exact example + query time range? might be a sampling or attribution bug.
anna: example: routeId=chat.autorespond, window=last_24h. panel shows a -$0.03 delta at 09:12. query I used:
```
SELECT route_id, time_bucket('1m', ts) as t, sum(net_cost) as cost
FROM route_costs_sample
WHERE route_id = 'chat.autorespond' AND ts >= now() - interval '24 hours'
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY 2
```
raj: thanks. quick guess: we might be subtracting a prefetch credit in tenant-level ledger while the route-level panel shows net of cache credit. double-counting or mis-attribution window.
phil: yup — we've got two overlapping credit pools: prefetch_credits (assigned to caller tenant) and cache_savings (assigned to the route hotpath). When a request gets routed sticky -> fallback, prefetch stays on tenant but cache_savings moves, making the route look like it "owes" money.
jordyn: saw this too during the Canary 2 rollout. users flipped routing and the dashboard showed negative marginal costs which freaked them out. was going to post. :hand_over_mouth:
raj: UX fix options:
- show a warning pill when sparkline includes mixed attribution windows
- add a toggle "include tenant-level prefetch credits"
- keep current but ~fix backend attribution
Which do we want short-term?
anna: short-term: toggle + tooltip. long-term: backend consistent attribution. the toggle buys us time for API/DB changes.
phil: implementation note — backend change is non-trivial: econ-service currently emits per-invocation rows with fields: route_id, tenant_id, token_count, cache_credit_applied boolean, prefetch_credit boolean. we'd need to add an attribution_key and a stable amortization_id to join credits across route hops. that touches ingestion and the ingestion QL.
raj: alternative: extend /econs/v1/route_stats to return both net_cost and exposure_breakdown array instead of creating a new endpoint. pros: single call for console; cons: bigger payload and more front-end parsing.
phil: I'm +1 for extending existing endpoint as long as we keep response backward-compatible (add optional field exposure_breakdown). else we end up supporting two endpoints forever.
jordyn: front-end notes: if we add exposure_breakdown it should come with human labels and confidence flags (sampled vs exact). Also probably a small legend explaining "why negative" cases with a hover.
anna: UX sketch (super tiny):
- sparkline line (net)
- small stacked area under it showing prefetch vs cache vs kernel amortization (hover shows numbers)
- toggle to "show raw exposures"
raj: backend rollout plan idea:
1) Emit exposure_breakdown in econ-service as opt-in flag (default false) for a week of canary traffic.
2) Console CLI /console-service fetches with flag for canary users.
3) If metrics look stable, flip default and drop legacy paths.
This lets us A/B test without blowing up DB.
phil: implementation caveats:
- sampling: we fingerprint tokens at emit time and we only do detailed exposure for 1/10000 requests to control cardinality. for non-sampled rows we return estimated breakdowns which are aggregated. need to surface that in API (confidence: low/med/high).
- storage: per-invocation expanded rows increase storage ~x6; we should only persist aggregates for 7 days.
anna: sounds reasonable. can we also surface an "explain" endpoint for a single invocation id so support can debug a negative spike?
phil: yeah, add /econs/v1/invocation/:id/explain that returns sampled provenance and join keys. gated to internal role.
raj: back to toggle: front-end also needs an affordance for "show tenant view" vs "route view" because some customers want their prefetched credits on the same chart. maybe a small dropdown: [Route net | Route w/tenant credits | Tenant net].
jordyn: +1. also let's default to the safer "Route net" (what customers expected in demo) and put a tooltip explaining differences.
anna: ok next actions:
- phil: create RFC PR for exposure_breakdown payload + sampling semantics (link in thread)
- raj: update console ticket to add toggle + legend copy
- jordyn: mock 2 variations (stacked area vs split-sparkline) and post screenshots
- anna: I'll write a small incident note for the demo and drop a recording.
phil: I started the RFC branch, will push a draft by EOD. note: need input from storage team about retention.
ops-bot: deploybot: econ-service/feature/exposure-breakdown pushed to canary cluster at 2024-09-10T15:23Z :rocket:
raj: awesome — once phil pushes link I can wire the UI to the opt-in flag and spin the 5% canary.
jordyn: thanks all. small reminder: add an explanation blurb in the Console docs so Product doesn't get CS tickets. :memo:
